top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks (Katori, Ye) are a mature, independently confirmed achievement: magic-wavelength trapping resolved the conflict between tight confinement and a narrow transition, and several laboratories (JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, SYRTE, NIST) now agree at the 1e-18 level, which is the independent confirmation I require. The credit is clean, one originator of the scheme and one leader in demonstrated performance, and the citation scope is precise. IceCube is a genuine discovery in my own field, but its attribution to three names is more contestable in a large collaboration, so it ranks second, ahead of no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; I am an astroparticle experimentalist with no profile-based tie to the lattice clock laureates, and my PAMELA, Fermi-LAT and XL-Calibur collaborations are not IceCube
